text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 2.6% today to $383, continuing a sharp five-day rally that's added 8% since August 25. The move is directly tied to oil prices hitting $90 per barrel following U.S. military strikes against Iran on September 1st—geopolitical tension in the Middle East is pushing crude higher, which improves refining margins (the profit refiners make by converting crude into gasoline and diesel). With U.S. refineries already running at 97.4% capacity, higher oil prices mean Marathon can sell finished fuel products at prices that have risen even faster than its raw material costs.

The broader context here is a collision of tight supply and political risk. The U.S. meeting with refining executives about high fuel prices (announced August 28) underscores how much geopolitical disruption in the Middle East is reshaping energy markets—and refiners like Marathon are positioned to benefit from the price spread between crude and products when Middle East tensions keep prices elevated. Combined with strong refinery utilization rates, this is a favorable environment for Marathon's core business.
